Key Duties and Responsibilities

The successful applicant will:
•	Inspect damaged vehicles and assess structural and panel damage.
•	Review repair specifications, job cards and insurance instructions to determine repair requirements.
•	Remove damaged panels, trims, bumpers, lights and associated components to gain access to damaged areas.
•	Repair damaged body panels using recognised panel beating techniques including reshaping, shrinking, stretching and pulling.
•	Straighten vehicle bodies, chassis and structural components using mechanical, hydraulic and electronic alignment equipment.

•	Remove and replace damaged panels and structural sections using new, recycled or fabricated components where required.

•	Identify additional damage and report variations to the Workshop Manager or estimator.
•	Complete job records accurately and maintain workshop documentation.
•	Operate and maintain workshop tools and equipment safely while following workplace health, safety and environmental procedures.
•	Work cooperatively with painters, estimators, mechanics, insurers and other workshop staff to achieve repair timeframes and quality outcomes.
•	Participate in ongoing training relating to new vehicle construction, repair methods and manufacturer standards.

Qualifications and Experience

•	An AQF Certificate III in Automotive Body Repair Technology (Panel Beating) or an equivalent recognised trade qualification
•	An overseas qualification assessed as comparable to the relevant Australian trade qualification; and
•	At least two years' relevant practical panel beating experience.
•	Applicants without the specified qualification may also be considered where they have at least three years' full-time industry experience in a similar environment.

Required Skills

•	Strong panel beating and collision repair skills.
•	Experience repairing structural and non-structural vehicle damage.
•	Competence in vehicle body measuring, chassis alignment and panel replacement.
•	Experience with automotive welding, cutting, bonding and fabrication techniques.
•	Ability to work with steel, aluminium, fibreglass and plastic vehicle components.
•	Competence using hydraulic pulling equipment, welders, grinders and other panel repair tools.
•	Ability to read repair specifications, technical information and job documentation.
•	Knowledge of manufacturer-approved repair methods and modern vehicle construction.
•	High attention to detail with a commitment to producing quality repairs safely and efficiently.

Personal Attributes

•	Reliable, punctual and professional.
•	Safety-conscious with a strong commitment to quality workmanship.
•	Able to work independently and as part of a team.
•	Well organised with the ability to prioritise work and meet deadlines.
•	Physically capable of performing the inherent requirements of the role.

Other Requirements

•	Any relevant trade licences or certifications where required.
•	The right to work in Australia or eligibility to obtain an appropriate visa.
•	Willingness to comply with company policies and pre-employment requirements.
